entries.name: German Iris
entries.summary: German Iris (Iris) is an aromatic in Book I of De Materia Medica. Modern identification: Iris germanica. Dioscorides discusses the root, leaf, flower, stalk. Preparations he mentions include decoction, infusion, in wine, with honey, with vinegar. He describes it as warming, softening, laxative. He lists uses relating to sores and wounds, aches and swellings, coughs, the chest and the throat, the skin, sleep and the nerves. A historical herbal entry. It is not used in our recipes unless it is a familiar culinary food.

entries.name: Melan
entries.summary: Melan (Melan) is a mineral or earth in Book V of De Materia Medica. Preparations he mentions include infusion, in wine, with honey, with vinegar, poultice/plaster. He describes it as warming, cooling, astringent, softening. He lists uses relating to sores and wounds, bites and poisons, the stomach and digestion, aches and swellings, the eyes. Not a food. Recorded for history only.
